from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Classical bits exist as either 0 or 1.",
            "Quantum states live in a complex Hilbert space.",
            "Imagine a toggle switch versus a dimmer knob.",
            "The dimmer represents infinite states between ON and OFF.",
            "This defines the basis of quantum superposition."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Classical vs. Quantum Divide", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        switch_0 = Square(color=WHITE).add(Text("0", font_size=24, color=WHITE))
        switch_1 = Square(color=WHITE).add(Text("1", font_size=24, color=WHITE))
        switches = VGroup(switch_0, switch_1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1)
        
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(switches, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(switches))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(switches), GrowFromCenter(sphere))
        self.play(sphere.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(BLUE).reverse_direction())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        path = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/2)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.play(Indicate(sphere), Indicate(dot))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining Superposition via Dirac Notation", [
            "Superposition follows the state vector formula.",
            "State vector equals alpha times 0 plus beta times 1.",
            "Alpha and beta are complex probability amplitudes.",
            "A spinning coin embodies this combined state.",
            "The weights of 0 and 1 change dynamically."
        ])

        # --- Assets ---
        # Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle = \alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle", color=YELLOW)
        
        # Gauge Bars
        gauge0 = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLUE)
        gauge1 = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=RED)
        label0 = MathTex(r"|0\rangle")
        label1 = MathTex(r"|1\rangle")
        
        # Spinning coin (placeholder)
        coin = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B3', 'B6', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(gauge0, 'D3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(gauge1, 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(label0, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(gauge0), Create(gauge1), Write(label0), Write(label1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(coin, 'F4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(coin))
        self.play(Rotate(coin, angle=2*PI, run_time=2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Animate weights
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        gauge0.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_height(2 * tracker.get_value()))
        gauge1.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_height(2 * (1 - tracker.get_value())))
        
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(0.8), run_time=2)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(0.2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Born rule governs probability calculations.",
            "The squares of amplitudes must sum to one.",
            "Measurement forces the system into one basis state.",
            "Schrödinger's cat provides our intuitive analogy.",
            "Opening the box collapses the wavefunction instantly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Measurement: The Collapse of the Wavefunction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        born_rule = MathTex(r"|\alpha|^2 + |\beta|^2 = 1", color=ORANGE)
        superposition = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).add(
            Dot(color=BLUE)
        )
        superposition_blur = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.5 + i*0.05, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.1) for i in range(3)
        ])
        superposition_visual = VGroup(superposition, superposition_blur)
        
        sharp_state = Dot(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.play(Write(born_rule))
        self.place_at_grid(born_rule, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(superposition_visual, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(superposition_visual))
        self.play(Rotate(superposition_visual, angle=2*PI, run_time=2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        flash = Rectangle(width=8, height=6, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sharp_state, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(superposition_visual),
            FadeIn(sharp_state)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(flash), FadeOut(flash), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Quantum States: The Bloch Sphere", [
            "The Bloch sphere maps these quantum states.",
            "Complex coefficients define points on the surface.",
            "Superposition is a rotation in this space."
        ])
        
        # --- Create objects ---
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, fill_opacity=0.2, color=WHITE).set_style(stroke_width=1)
        # 3D representation is tricky in 2D grid, using Circles as proxy
        bloch_viz = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE),
            Line(UP*1.5, DOWN*1.5, color=GRAY),
            Line(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, color=GRAY)
        )
        
        north_label = Text("|0⟩", color="#00FF00", font_size=20).next_to(UP*1.5, UP, buff=0.1)
        south_label = Text("|1⟩", color="#00FF00", font_size=20).next_to(DOWN*1.5, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        state_point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        state_label = Text("ψ", color=YELLOW, font_size=20).next_to(state_point, UR, buff=0.1)
        state_group = VGroup(state_point, state_label)
        
        # Initialize
        self.place_in_area(bloch_viz, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(bloch_viz), Write(north_label), Write(south_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(state_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        # Show rotation simulation
        path = Arc(radius=1.0, start_angle=PI/4, angle=PI/2, color=RED)
        self.play(Rotate(state_group, angle=PI/2, about_point=bloch_viz.get_center()), Create(path))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", [
            "Superposition allows simultaneous processing of possibilities.",
            "Quantum computers explore all paths at once.",
            "Quantum reality is fundamentally 'both/and' logic."
        ])

outline.topic: Superposition and Quantum States: The Mechanics of 'Both/And'

sections.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
sections.content: Establish the prerequisite: classical bits are binary (0 or 1). Introduce the concept of a state vector in Hilbert space. Use a visual 'toggle switch' to represent classical states, contrasting it with a 'spherical bloom' for quantum states.
sections.example: A classical light switch (ON/OFF) vs. a dimmer switch knob that can be adjusted to any angle between ON and OFF.

sections.title: Defining Superposition via Dirac Notation
sections.content: Introduce the superposition principle mathematically: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩. Explain that α and β are probability amplitudes (complex numbers). Use a visual gauge bar showing the 'weight' of state 0 and state 1 changing dynamically as the vector rotates.
sections.example: Representing a spinning coin: while spinning, it is neither purely heads nor tails, but a linear combination of both.

sections.title: Measurement: The Collapse of the Wavefunction
sections.content: Explain the Born Rule: |α|² + |β|² = 1. Describe how the act of measurement forces the system to choose one basis state. Use a 'camera flash' animation: the blurred 'spin' freezes instantly into a single state.
sections.example: Schrödinger’s Cat: The box represents the superposition; opening the lid is the measurement that forces the outcome into a definitive 'Alive' or 'Dead' state.

sections.title: Visualizing Quantum States: The Bloch Sphere
sections.content: Synthesize the previous points using the Bloch Sphere. Map the complex coefficients onto a 3D coordinate system. Show that any point on the surface of the sphere is a valid quantum state, emphasizing that superposition is a rotation in this space.
sections.example: A laser pointer beam aiming at different spots on a translucent sphere, where every spot represents a unique superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Conclude by bridging theory to computing. Explain that superposition allows quantum computers to process multiple possibilities simultaneously. Reiterate the 'Both/And' nature of quantum reality.
sections.example: A maze-solving robot that doesn't walk one path at a time, but instead 'fills' all paths simultaneously, collapsing to the correct exit only upon discovery.
